world.era: 1692 (Salem Village, Massachusetts Bay Colony); 1953-56 for Miller's McCarthy-era frame
world.setting: Salem Village and Salem Town, Massachusetts, 1692: the woods, the parsonage, Puritan farmhouses, the meetinghouse court, the jail and Gallows Hill; plus the 1950s HUAC hearings Miller wrote against
world.register: period documentary realism, 1692 New England Puritans: candlelight, grey wool and white linen, bare timber, cold dawn

parris.name: Reverend Samuel Parris
parris.role: Salem's insecure minister, Betty's father, Abigail's uncle; fears losing his pulpit
parris.look: a gaunt middle-aged Puritan minister in a plain black coat and white preaching bands, thinning dark hair, anxious pinched face, Salem Village 1692

abigail.name: Abigail Williams
abigail.role: Parris's orphaned niece, seventeen, Proctor's former lover and the leading accuser
abigail.look: a striking young Puritan woman with long dark hair escaping a white linen cap, plain grey wool dress with a white collar and apron, intense dark eyes, Salem 1692

betty.name: Betty Parris
betty.role: Parris's young daughter who lies unresponsive after the forest night
betty.look: a pale ten-year-old Puritan girl with fair hair under a white nightcap, white linen nightgown, lying still in a wooden bed, Salem 1692

tituba.name: Tituba
tituba.role: enslaved woman from Barbados in Parris's household; first to confess and name others
tituba.look: a Black woman in her forties from Barbados, dark skin, a faded red headscarf, a coarse brown wool dress and shawl, Salem 1692

proctor.name: John Proctor
proctor.role: farmer, Elizabeth's husband, Abigail's former lover; dies rather than sign his name to a lie
proctor.look: a broad-shouldered Puritan farmer in his thirties, dark unruly hair and short beard, rough brown linen shirt with rolled sleeves and a leather work vest, Salem 1692

elizabeth.name: Elizabeth Proctor
elizabeth.role: John's wife; never lies, tells one lie to protect him
elizabeth.look: a composed Puritan wife in her thirties, brown hair hidden under a white linen coif, dark blue wool dress with a plain white collar and apron, restrained grave expression, Salem 1692

thomas-putnam.name: Thomas Putnam
thomas-putnam.role: wealthy, bitter landowner who signs the first complaints and buys forfeited land
thomas-putnam.look: a heavy-set wealthy Puritan landowner in his forties, florid face, grey-streaked hair, a fine dark green wool coat with pewter buttons and a wide-brimmed black hat, Salem 1692

ann-putnam.name: Ann Putnam
ann-putnam.role: Thomas's wife, who buried seven babies and blames witchcraft
ann-putnam.look: a hollow-eyed Puritan woman in her late thirties in a black mourning dress and black hood, pale grief-worn face, Salem 1692

rebecca.name: Rebecca Nurse
rebecca.role: respected elderly woman of the Nurse family, accused and hanged
rebecca.look: a gentle white-haired Puritan grandmother in her seventies, lined kind face, grey wool dress, white shawl and white linen cap, Salem 1692

giles.name: Giles Corey
giles.role: cantankerous old farmer who knows the law; stays mute to keep his land for his sons
giles.look: a wiry, weathered farmer in his eighties, white stubble beard and bald crown, patched brown farm coat and breeches, Salem 1692

hale.name: Reverend John Hale
hale.role: learned witch-hunter from Beverly who comes to doubt the court
hale.look: a scholarly Puritan clergyman in his late thirties, clean-shaven earnest face, black clerical coat and white bands, carrying a stack of heavy leather books, Massachusetts 1692

danforth.name: Deputy Governor Danforth
danforth.role: presiding judge who protects the court's authority
danforth.look: a stern grey-haired colonial judge in his sixties in a black judicial robe with white bands and a long powdered periwig, cold heavy-lidded eyes, Massachusetts 1692

mary-warren.name: Mary Warren
mary-warren.role: the Proctors' timid servant girl, who sews the poppet and later tries to testify
mary-warren.look: a timid, mousy eighteen-year-old servant girl with light brown hair under a white cap, a plain brown wool dress and patched apron, Salem 1692

cheever.name: Ezekiel Cheever
cheever.role: court clerk who serves the warrant and finds the needle
cheever.look: a thin, officious court clerk in his forties in a dark brown coat, a black hat and a leather satchel of papers, Salem 1692

girls.name: the Salem girls
girls.look: a group of four Puritan teenage girls in grey and brown wool dresses with white caps and aprons, wide frightened eyes, Salem 1692

sarah-good.name: Sarah Good
sarah-good.role: a homeless beggar woman, among the first named by Tituba
sarah-good.look: a ragged, homeless middle-aged woman in a torn dark shawl and soiled skirts, tangled grey hair, Salem 1692

miller.name: Arthur Miller
miller.role: the playwright, who wrote The Crucible in 1953 and later refused to name names before HUAC
miller.look: a tall lean American playwright in his late thirties with dark wavy hair and black horn-rimmed glasses, a 1950s grey suit and narrow tie, 1950s America

salemForest.look: the pitch-black Massachusetts woods at night in 1692, bare trees lit by a sputtering smoky fire under a boiling iron kettle

parrisBedroom.look: a cramped candlelit upstairs bedroom in a 1692 Puritan parsonage, a narrow wooden bed under a small leaded window

proctorFarmhouse.look: the dim common room of a 1692 Puritan farmhouse, a wide hearth fire, a plain plank table, a wooden mantel

meetinghouse.look: the unheated Salem Village meetinghouse, bare timber walls, rows of plain wooden benches, breath visible in the cold

courtroom.look: the Salem 1692 courtroom in the meetinghouse, judges at a raised bench in black robes, crowded benches, high rafters

salemJail.look: a dark stone-and-timber Salem jail cell at dawn, straw on the floor, a barred window, a small table with paper and quill

gallowsHill.look: a rocky hill outside Salem at grey dawn in 1692, an oxcart on a dirt track and a crowd of townsfolk

huacHearing.look: a 1950s Washington congressional hearing room, a committee on a raised dais, microphones, a lone witness at a table

objects.why: the court, warrants, indictments and the confession bargain at the heart of the thesis
the written confession Proctor signs and tears; the warrant; Giles Corey's deposition
the Devil's black book the accused must claim to have signed; Hale's heavy books
land as currency: forfeited farms auctioned off, the Putnam land grab, the Nurses' 300 acres
the hangings on Gallows Hill and Ann Putnam's seven buried babies
the forest fire under the kettle; Hale's 'whole green world burning'
the performed confession and the girls' theatre in court
Abigail controlling the girls and the court; Putnam directing his wife's grief
the church door where Danforth wants the confession nailed
Parris and Betty; the Proctor marriage; Giles Corey's sons

spine.claim: In 1692 Salem the truth hanged you and a confession saved you, so the town was not mad: people responded rationally to a court with inverted incentives, and John Proctor's real crisis is his name.
Each player protects their standing: Parris his pulpit after the forest night, Abigail her prize by terrorising the girls, Thomas Putnam his acreage through accusations that make land forfeit.

Tituba's confession prints the court's price list, Abigail turns Mary Warren's poppet and needle into planted evidence, and in court the truth itself becomes a threat: Proctor confesses adultery and Elizabeth's one lie damns them both.
Giles Corey defeats the rigged game by staying silent to keep his land for his sons, and on the last morning Proctor signs a confession, then tears it rather than let his name be nailed to a lie.

Miller rewrote history (Abigail was 11, Proctor 60) to indict the McCarthy hearings, and the lesson holds: a system that pays people to lie will always find liars, and the only defence is someone who will not sell their name.
